sections.label: Rise in deepfake incidents
sections.summary: Deepfake incidents have increased noticeably in countries with elections, including India, Indonesia and South Korea.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, there has been a noticeable increase of deepfake incidents in countries where elections have taken place or are planned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In India, compared to a year ago, there are three times as many deepfake incidents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In Indonesia, more than 15 times; and in South Korea, more than 16 times.

sections.label: South Korea election law
sections.summary: South Korea revised its Public Official Election Act to ban AI-generated campaign videos 90 days before an election, with penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, South Korea revised its Public Official Election Act to ban political campaign videos that use AI-generated content 90 days prior to an election.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Violations of the revised law, which took effect in January this year, can lead to jail time of up to seven years or a fine of up to 50 million won, which is almost $50,000.

sections.label: California deepfake deception law
sections.summary: California passed a law requiring social media platforms to block deceptive deepfakes of candidates from 120 days before an election.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Last month, the state of California passed into law the "Defending Democracy from Deepfake Deception Act of 2024", which requires social media platforms to block materially deceptive deepfakes of candidates from 120 days before the election to the day of the election.

sections.label: ELIONA Bill purpose
sections.summary: The ELIONA Bill augments election laws under the Parliamentary Elections Act and Presidential Elections Act to uphold candidate truthfulness and election integrity.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Bill, or ELIONA Bill, is our carefully calibrated response to augment our election laws under the Parliamentary Elections Act and the Presidential Elections Act, ensuring that the truthfulness of candidate representation and the integrity of our elections continue to be upheld.

sections.label: Prohibited content conditions
sections.summary: Content is prohibited if it meets four legal limbs, and publishing it during the election period is an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In this regard, the law will apply so long as there are some members of the public who would reasonably believe that the candidate did say or do what was depicted.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Also, in assessing whether content matches a candidate's speech or actions, we will be relying primarily on declarations by the candidate if he or she had said or done that thing.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: All four legal limbs have to be met for the content to be prohibited.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: That is, the content: (a) is or includes OEA; (b) is digitally generated or manipulated; and (c) depicts a candidate saying or doing something that he or she did not, in fact, say or do; (d) but is realistic enough that some members of the public who see or hear the content would reasonably believe that the candidate did, in fact, say or do that thing.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Examples of content that would be prohibited include: (a) realistic audiofakes featuring a candidate saying things he did not say; (b) realistic AI-generated images of a candidate participating at events that did not happen, meeting people that he or she did not meet; and (c) realistic manipulated images or videos taken out of context and misrepresenting a candidate's actions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The publication of such prohibited content during the election period, including by boosting, sharing and reposting existing content, will be an offence.

sections.label: Prospective candidate identification
sections.summary: From the Writ to Nomination Day, a two-part requirement is introduced for individuals identifying themselves as prospective candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From the issuance of the Writ to Nomination Day, we will introduce a two-part requirement for individuals who would like to identify themselves as prospective candidates and have the safeguards of the ELIONA Bill apply to them.

sections.label: ELIONA Bill candidate content safeguards
sections.summary: The ELIONA Bill safeguards apply to content depicting all successfully nominated candidates from the end of nomination proceedings until polling closes on Polling Day.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: After nomination proceedings are completed and up to the close of polling on Polling Day, the safeguards of the ELIONA Bill will apply to content depicting all successfully nominated candidates.

sections.label: Funding for online harms detection
sections.summary: $50 million over five years goes to CATOS to develop technological capabilities to detect online harms, including harmful digitally manipulated content.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Continuing strong investment in research is one way to ensure we stay ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have channelled $50 million in funding over five years to CATOS, which will develop new technological capabilities to detect online harms, including harmful digitally manipulated content.

sections.label: False declaration in takedown requests
sections.summary: It will be an illegal practice for candidates to knowingly make a false or misleading declaration in a request to take down content.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To deter abuse of the law, such as candidates requesting to take down unfavourable content that is, in fact, a factual representation of their speech or action, it will be made an illegal practice for candidates to knowingly make a false or misleading declaration in a request.

sections.label: Fine for social media non-compliance
sections.summary: The fine for a social media service provider that fails to comply with a corrective direction has been raised to up to $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Recognising the extensive reach and responsibility that social media services must uphold, we have raised the fine of up to $1 million for a provider of a social media service that fails to comply with a corrective direction.

sections.label: Application during election period
sections.summary: It applies only during the election period, from issuance of the Writ to the end of polling on Polling Day.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Second, it applies only during the election period, from the issuance of the Writ to the end of polling on Polling Day, to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process and preserve space for fair and legitimate political discourse during the elections.

sections.label: Direction to remove deepfakes
sections.summary: The Minister or Alternate Authority may direct removal or disabling of access to deepfakes containing false statements of fact when in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Minister or Alternate Authority may also direct the removal or disabling of access to deepfakes on the grounds that they contain false statements of fact and it is in the public interest to issue the direction.

sections.label: POFMA code for social media
sections.summary: Major social media services are prescribed Internet intermediaries and will face an upcoming POFMA Code of Practice on digitally generated or manipulated content, targeted for 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Most major social media services are also prescribed Internet intermediaries (PIIs) under POFMA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They will be required to prevent and counter the abuse of digitally generated or manipulated content at all times through an upcoming Code of Practice under POFMA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Like the three other POFMA codes in effect today, the new Code is being formulated in consultation with the PIIs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We intend to finalise the Code for issuance in 2025.

sections.label: Law against fake election content
sections.summary: The new law aims to prohibit online publication of fake content distorting a candidate's speech or actions, to protect the democratic process and election fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In recent elections held in several countries, we have already witnessed the harm caused by fake content.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This new law aims to prohibit the online publication of fake content that distorts a candidate's speech or actions so that we can better protect our democratic process and the fairness of our elections.

sections.label: Private communications exemption in clause 2
sections.summary: Clause 2, section 61a states the offence does not apply to private and domestic communications, though many political messages are not created by parties or candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under clause 2, section 61a, it states that this offence does not apply to "private and domestic communications." Yet, many political messages are not created by political parties or candidates themselves.

sections.label: Fake accounts and deepfakes question
sections.summary: The Member asks how the Bill will address fake accounts and deepfakes from private accounts and messaging channels, since harm could occur before anything is reported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The harm could be done before anything is reported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, can the Minister clarify how the Bill will address fake accounts and deepfakes from these private accounts and messaging channels?

sections.label: Content types considered offences
sections.summary: The Member asks the Minister to elaborate on the specific types of content that would be considered an offence under this law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister elaborate on the specific types of content that would be considered an offence under this law?

sections.label: Follow-up during nine-day campaign
sections.summary: The Member asks how the Ministry will ensure timely follow-up on such requests given the extremely short nine-day election campaign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, given the extremely short nine-day election campaign, how will the Ministry ensure timely follow-up on such requests?

sections.label: Bill coverage before election writ
sections.summary: The Bill applies only after the Writ of Election is issued, though misleading content can circulate earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill's provisions apply only after the Writ of Election is issued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, misleading or manipulated content could circulate long before the campaign period begins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given that election advertising can start unofficially well before the writ is issued, why does the Bill only cover the period after the writ is issued?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Moreover, with a condensed nine-day campaign period, what assurances can the Minister provide regarding timely and decisive enforcement?

sections.label: Workers' Party support for Bill
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the Bill to combat digitally manipulated media, while raising two main concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party (WP) therefore supports the introduction of legislation to combat the threat of digitally manipulated media contained in this amendment Bill, although I wish to raise two main areas of concern and seek further clarifications from the Minister on other further technical points.

sections.label: Accountability for outlets and codes
sections.summary: It asks what mechanisms hold outlets accountable for prohibited content and when new codes will be published.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What mechanisms will be in place to hold these outlets accountable if they do publish or propagate prohibited content, intentionally or unintentionally?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Would there thus also be new codes or updates to the existing codes of practice, such as the promised new code of conduct which the Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) states will be published to ensure social media companies do more to moderate content and when is the expected publication date?

sections.label: Criteria for private communications exemption
sections.summary: It asks what criteria determine whether a communication is private and exempt from the Bill's prohibitions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What are the criteria to be used to determine whether or not a specific communication is private and therefore exempt from the prohibitions contained in the Bill?

sections.label: Prohibited content outside election period
sections.summary: It asks how prohibited content aimed at influencing political sentiment is treated outside an official election period.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While it is necessarily the way it is scoped because the acts being amended are acts governing our two types of elections in Singapore, what is the treatment regulating prohibited content aimed at influencing political sentiment when we are not in an official election period?

sections.label: Sufficiency of platform fines
sections.summary: It notes the $1 million maximum fine for platforms might be questioned as sufficient to compel trillion-dollar companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After all, for platforms, the maximum fine of $1 million dollars might be questioned about whether it was sufficient to compel trillion-dollar companies, such as Meta and TikTok to comply.

sections.label: Positive deepfakes and false reports
sections.summary: Asks whether positive deepfakes fall under the prohibition and what penalty applies to a member of the public making a false report.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Would these cases of "positive deepfakes" fall under the scope of the prohibition?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Also, given that anyone can make a report, what is the penalty if a member of the public makes a false report?

sections.label: Media literacy and deepfake concerns
sections.summary: Proposes media literacy education and short-form content, supports election deepfake measures, and seeks clarifications from the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Specific proposals could include enhancing media literacy education in schools and other touchpoints, where our citizens hone their critical thinking skills necessary to navigate the increasingly complex information landscape.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We can also use short-form content on social media and interactive online experiences to reach a wide audience, teaching them to recognise common manipulation techniques used in deepfakes and other types of misinformation campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To conclude, we support the addition of measures to tackle the harm that deepfakes and such manipulated content can cause during the especially vulnerable period of an election campaign.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, I believe that there are a number of concerns and clarifications that I hope the Minister can address, as we work together to ensure that our democratic process does not come under threat by sophisticated manipulated media.

sections.label: Defining the election period
sections.summary: Notes the Bill targets deepfakes during the election period but the election period is not clearly stated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: My first, on defining the election period, the Bill targets deepfake deployed during the election period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, what exactly is the election period is not so clearly stated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I heard Minister Josephine Teo stating in the Second Reading speech earlier, that the election period begins from the issuance of the rate of elections until the close of polling day.

sections.label: Other tools beyond election deepfakes
sections.summary: States that defamation laws, POFMA and OCHA address deepfakes in non-election contexts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While we must act to prevent malicious use of deepfakes during elections, we have other tools, such as defamation laws, the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act, or POFMA, and the Online Criminal Harms Act, or OCHA, to address such issues and deepfakes in non-election context.

sections.label: Defences under clause 2
sections.summary: Describes the defence of not knowing the representation was untrue and exemptions for private communications, authorised news agencies and prescribed circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under clause 2 of the explanatory statement of the Bill, it is a defence for an individual to prove that they did not know and had no reason to believe the representation of a candidate was, in fact, untrue and that the offence does not apply to private and domestic communications, the publication of news by authorised news agencies and other prescribed circumstances.

sections.label: Labelled fake deepfakes still harm
sections.summary: States a labelled fake video still caused significant damage, satire and parody are allowed with disclosure, and Singapore lacks a full satire defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The video, though clearly marked as fake, was widely viewed and caused significant damage before it was taken down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This demonstrates that even when deepfakes are labelled as fake or satire, they can still cause harm, particularly in the short timeframe of an election period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, election communications that contain materially deceptive content which constitutes satire or parody and containing such disclosure that the content has been manipulated for the purposes of satire or parody would be allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, in Singapore, we do not have a full defence for satire and parody.

sections.label: Bill coverage gap
sections.summary: The Bill does not cover such instances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, the Bill does not cover such instances.

sections.label: Deepfakes threaten democracy
sections.summary: Deepfakes can be weaponised to undermine democracy, distort truth and damage election reputations, so legal safeguards are needed to protect democratic values and candidates' families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Deepfakes, if left unchecked, can be weaponised to undermine our democracy, distort the truth and damage the reputation of our elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is crucial that we act now to put in place the necessary legal safeguards to protect our democratic values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Quite apart from the political arena, we must remember that candidates have their own lives, their own families, their own children, career, organisations and loved ones, all of whom will be impacted by such false information long after the dust of election has settled and long after the heat of hustings have cooled down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us ensure that, in Singapore, what is said about our elections and our candidates is rooted in truth, integrity and respect for our democratic process, ensuring that truth, not deception, guides our democratic processes.

sections.label: Publishing deepfake videos offence
sections.summary: The Bill makes it an offence to publish such videos, but not to create them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, this Bill makes it an offence for any person to publish or cause to be published such videos.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Notably though, this Bill does not make it an automatic offence to create such a video, but only to publish it.

sections.label: Stronger penalties and bot accounts
sections.summary: The speaker suggests stronger penalties for content creators, notes bot accounts may fall outside the Bill, and describes section 61MA criminalising publication of digitally generated candidate representations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Second, I think there is scope for significantly more serious and even punitive penalties to be imposed against the creators of the contents themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think the current penalties of a fine of $1,000 and imprisonment not exceeding 12 months suggest that this is to be treated as a minor offence, with no distinction made for creators of content and those who may just publish it on their platform by sharing a link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think we may also have to deal with a situation where content may be published and circulated by bot accounts and perhaps even substantially generated by such accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Such publications may be outside the scope of this Bill and that would mean taking action against such accounts or even social media platforms more difficult, because the primary offence is not triggered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Although I know most platforms have internal rules that require natural people to operate the individual accounts, this is not currently a matter that is regulated and there are many reports of a large number of bot accounts that operate on social media platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Overall, though, I think this is an important legislation that takes concrete measures in helping to combat the insidious use of AI to undermine candidates and manipulate elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think there is scope for even stronger measures against the threat and would suggest that these measures be continuously evaluated and improved as needed to combat this threat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Among other amendments, this Bill introduces section 61MA, which criminalises the publication of OEA that contains realistic representations created using content that was digitally generated or manipulated of a candidate saying or doing something that he or she did not, in fact, say or do.

sections.label: Deepfake incidents involving leaders
sections.summary: Lee Hsien Loong, Lawrence Wong, Vivian Balakrishnan, Tan Wu Meng, Edward Chia and Yip Hon Weng were portrayed in deepfakes or manipulated photos.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In December last year, then-Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong was portrayed in a deepfake video promoting a cryptocurrency scam.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Also in December last year, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong was shown endorsing an investment scam.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In April this year, Foreign Affairs Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, along with other Members, Dr Tan Wu Meng, Mr Edward Chia and Mr Yip Hon Weng, each received an extortion letter containing a manipulated photo.

sections.label: Public education on fake messages
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MDDI plans educational activities to help the public identify AI-generated fake messages, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is far more important that the public is equipped with the ability to discern what is fake from real.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Hence, apart from passing this legislation, does the Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) plan to launch any educational activities in future to educate the public on how to identify AI-generated fake messages? : Mr Speaker, notwithstanding my clarifications, I stand in support of this Bill.

sections.label: AI deepfake election ban question
sections.summary: A 90-day ban on AI-generated political deepfakes was implemented before April elections, and the speaker asks why messaging app forwarding is excluded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Before its legislative elections in April this year, they implemented a 90-day ban on AI-generated deepfake content of a political nature.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to ask why forwarding via messaging apps is not included in the proposals.

sections.label: Forwarding fake content enforcement gap
sections.summary: The speaker says ill-intent actors may exploit the forwarding gap, notes enforcement practicality, and states the Returning Officer can issue corrective directions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Those with ill intent may exploit this gap in order to ensure that their fake content reaches the widest audience possible to impact the electoral results. : The practicality of enforcement actions may be a factor for consideration, but perhaps the Ministry would consider sending a clear signal that such content is banned and that forwarding them is an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is stated that the Returning Officer can issue corrective directions to individuals who publish such content, social media services and Internet Access Service Providers, to take down offending content or to disable access by Singapore users to such content during the election period.

sections.label: Handling influx overwhelming teams
sections.summary: The passage asks how teams will handle an influx, some maliciously designed to overwhelm the system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How will the teams handle situations where there could be an influx, with some maliciously designed to overwhelm the system?

sections.label: Bill against false representations
sections.summary: The Bill prohibits publication of realistic but false representations, particularly those manipulated through GenAI, to safeguard against misinformation and deepfakes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, with this shift comes the darker side – misinformation, deepfakes and digitally manipulated content designed to deceive and mislead voters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill is essential to safeguard against such threats by prohibiting the publication of realistic but false representations, particularly those manipulated through GenAI.

sections.label: Slovak election AI videos
sections.summary: During the 2023 Slovak elections, AI-generated videos spread on Facebook and Telegram falsely depicting a candidate discussing vote buying.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Similarly, during the 2023 Slovak elections, which the Minister mentioned earlier, AI-generated videos spread across platforms, like Facebook and Telegram, which include falsely depicting a candidate discussing vote buying.

sections.label: Platform fines for electoral integrity
sections.summary: Penalties up to $1 million for failing to act on corrective directions hold platforms accountable, and the speaker asks if this fine is fair or enough.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: By holding them accountable and imposing penalties up to $1 million for failing to act on corrective directions, we ensure that platforms share in the responsibility for maintaining electoral integrity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But then again, is $1 million fine truly fair or enough across the board?

sections.label: Support for election deepfake Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill tackling AI deepfakes and manipulated content, urging vigilance and societal rejection of misinformation to keep elections fair and trustworthy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While this Bill tackles AI-generated deepfakes and manipulated content, we must remain vigilant for new technologies that could be used to distort electoral processes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We must also collectively, as a society, be able to identify and reject misinformation and deepfakes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With this Bill, we reaffirm our commitment to a fair, transparent and trustworthy electoral system for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the concerns and clarifications raised, Sir, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Candidates requesting action on manipulated content
sections.summary: Under the Parliamentary Elections Act and Presidential Elections Act, candidates may ask the Returning Officer to act against manipulated online election advertising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under section 61N(2A) of the Parliamentary Elections Act and section 42LA(4) of the Presidential Elections Act, candidates may request the Returning Officer to take action against manipulated OEA.

sections.label: Corrective directions and realistic representation
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to confirm any candidate may request corrective directions, and the representation must be realistic enough for the public to reasonably believe the candidate said or did it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the avoidance of any doubt, can the Minister confirm if any candidate can request for corrective directions to be issued, not just candidates who are the subjects of the concerning content?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under section 61MA(1)(e) of the Parliamentary Elections Act and section 42LA(1)(e) of the Presidential Elections Act, the representation must be realistic enough that it is likely that some members of the general public would, if they heard or saw the representation, reasonably believe that the candidate said or did that thing.

sections.label: Private or domestic communications exemption
sections.summary: Under the Parliamentary Elections Act and Presidential Elections Act, the ban does not apply to communications of a private or domestic nature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under section 61MA(4) of the Parliamentary Elections Act and section 42LA(4) of the Presidential Elections Act, the ban does not apply to communications which are "of a private or domestic nature".

sections.label: Factors for private or domestic nature
sections.summary: The question asks what factors, besides the number of recipients, the Returning Officer will consider in deciding whether communications are private or domestic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What factors, aside from the number of persons receiving the communication, will the Returning Officer consider when determining whether the communications are "of a private or domestic nature"?

sections.label: Temporary political deepfake ban rejected
sections.summary: Responding to Ms Joan Pereira, the speaker says a temporary ban on all political deepfake content during elections was considered but decided unnecessary.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In response to Ms Joan Pereira’s question, we did consider a temporary ban on all deepfake content of a political nature during elections.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: After careful deliberations, we decided this was not necessary.

sections.label: Code of Practice safeguards
sections.summary: A Code of Practice will require specified social media services to implement safeguards beyond the election period in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Practically speaking, however, even if we wanted ELIONA to take effect x days before an election, we cannot do so until the Writ is issued and Polling Day revealed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is why we will introduce a Code of Practice to require specified social media services to implement safeguards beyond the election period specified in the Bill.

sections.label: AI-edited content not exempt
sections.summary: ELIONA does not exempt content partially edited by AI or traditional technology from prohibitions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This further blurs the line between content that has been purely manipulated via AI technology and other traditional means.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is why ELIONA does not exempt from prohibitions content that has been partially edited by AI or other more traditional technology.

sections.label: Four criteria for prohibited content
sections.summary: Content meeting four criteria will be prohibited even if labelled.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What matters are the four criteria I have shared previously: (a) the content constitutes OEA; (b) it is digitally generated or manipulated; (c) it is realistic; and (d) it shows the candidate doing what he did not do or saying what he did not say.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If these criteria are met, the content will be prohibited, even if labelled.

sections.label: Large chat groups not private
sections.summary: Large WhatsApp and Telegram chat groups anyone can join should not be considered private or domestic communication.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As an example, chat groups on WhatsApp and Telegram with very large memberships that anyone can freely join should not be considered private or domestic communication.

sections.label: Prohibiting believable deepfake content
sections.summary: The ELIONA Bill allows prohibition of deepfake content as long as some voters reasonably find them believable.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But why should we subject our elections to such risk at all, if we can prevent it or, at least, minimise it?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is why the ELIONA Bill has been drafted in this manner, to allow for the prohibition of deepfake content as long as some voters reasonably find them believable.

sections.label: Corrective direction and false declarations
sections.summary: Recipients of a corrective direction can contact the Returning Officer, and false declarations by a candidate carry serious consequences including loss of seat.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Recipients of a corrective direction who feel that their content has been wrongfully taken down can contact the Returning Officer to provide supporting evidence of their claims.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If content was found to have been mistakenly taken down due to a false declaration by a candidate, there will be serious consequences for the candidate, including the loss of his or her seat if elected.

sections.label: Corrective directions and deepfake ban
sections.summary: Corrective directions require responses within hours, and the proposed ban covers digitally generated or manipulated online election advertising depicting candidates published in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Once a corrective direction is issued, the expectation is for individuals, social media services and Internet access service providers to respond within hours.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The proposed ban covers the publication in Singapore of all digitally generated and manipulated OEA depicting candidates, regardless of the nationality of the user who created or published the content.

sections.label: Penalty for non-compliance
sections.summary: Non-compliance with corrective directions is an offence punishable by a fine of up to $1 million, with Courts deciding the level for each offence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Non-compliance with the corrective directions is an offence punishable by a fine of up to $1 million and it will be for the Courts to decide the appropriate level for each offence.

sections.label: Government deepfake detection tools
sections.summary: The Government will use commercially available and in-house tools, including AlchemiX, which compares recordings of a suspected deepfake video with a speaker's actual voice.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government will use a mix of commercially available and in-house tools such as AlchemiX, a tool developed by the Home Team Science and Technology Agency which can compare recordings of a suspected deepfake video with a recording of a speaker's actual voice.

sections.label: IMDA Code of Practice
sections.summary: IMDA will introduce a Code of Practice to deal with digitally manipulated content at all times, beyond election periods.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As I said in my opening speech, the IMDA will introduce a Code of Practice to deal with digitally manipulated content at all times, beyond the election periods.

sections.label: Code introduction in 2025
sections.summary: Companies have been receptive to the proposals and recognise the need to do more against digitally manipulated content, with the code aimed for introduction in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The companies have been receptive to our proposals and recognise the need to do more against digitally manipulated content.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We aim to introduce the code in 2025.

sections.label: AI-generated speech prohibition
sections.summary: The Bill offers no room for misunderstanding: using AI to generate a speech is prohibited if the person did not in fact read it out, even if they wrote it.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The video that I played earlier was completely generated by AI, notwithstanding the fact that the script was approved by me and it could have been penned by me, that image itself is problematic.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I did not actually stand in front a camera and articulate those words.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, the way the Bill is designed is to not offer any room for misunderstanding.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If you did not, in fact, read out a speech, even if you had written it, you used AI to generate that speech, that is prohibited.
